source: Mideksa Kebede, Compiled Body of Works in Field Epidemiology, Ethiopian FELTP, Addis Ababa University, June 2018 - Kolfe Keranyo sub-city cholera outbreak investigation, Addis Ababa, with national background figures for week 20 of 2016
processing_notes: Source states: 'Cholera outbreak is the continuous problem in the three regions of Ethiopia. As of week 20, 2016, a total of 1, 884 cholera cases and 19 deaths with CFR of 1.0% had been reported from three regions namely Oromiya, SNNP and Ethiopian Somali regions. [companion statement in three other Ethiopian FELTP theses: 'as of week 20, 2016, a total of 1,884 AWD cases and 19 deaths had been reported from eight zones in 25 woredas (districts) of three regions (from week 45/2015 up to week 20/2016)']' - interpreted as 1884 sCh cases, 19 deaths. AGENT 5 - RE-MINE OF THE AAU FELTP THESIS CORPUS. NATIONAL CUMULATIVE for the OPENING PHASE of Ethiopia's 2015-2017 epidemic: 1,884 cases and 19 deaths from epidemiological week 45 of 2015 to week 20 of 2016, across eight zones and 25 woredas of three regions (Oromia, SNNPR and Somali). CORROBORATED FOUR TIMES OVER, which is why it is committed despite being a thesis citation rather than a primary bulletin: the same figures appear independently in the Compiled Bodies of Works of Mideksa Kebede (2018), Girma Birhanu, Melaku Seyoum (2019) and a fourth resident, three of them giving the explicit week-45-2015-to-week-20-2016 window and one of them naming the three regions. ARITHMETIC CHECK: 19/1,884 = 1.008%, matching the printed CFR of 1.0%. DATES: ISO week 45 of 2015 began 2 November 2015 and week 20 of 2016 ended 22 May 2016. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE SHAPE OF THE EPIDEMIC: the national 2016 total is 29,871 (Index 1), so only 1,884 cases - about 6% - had accrued by late May 2016. The wave exploded in the second half of 2016. It also sits consistently on top of Agent 4's finding that the 2015 wave began in epidemiological WEEK 35 of 2015 and produced only 238 cases in Aug-Dec 2015 (Index 441-444). NATIONAL TOTAL and the primary count for its period - do not sum with sub-national rows for the same dates, nor with the calendar-year national rows for 2015 or 2016, which overlap it.
